# Tom Collins - Variation #2

- **Source:** House of Bitter Bear / Anders Erickson, [Tom Collins - Variation #2](https://houseofbitterbear.com/collections/tom-collins-variation-2). Accessed 2026-09-27.
- **Version:** Published source specification; instructions condensed. Quantity assumptions and source issues are noted below.
- **Yield:** 1 cocktail (serving assumption where the source omits yield).
- **Recipe text:** [Publisher recipe index](https://houseofbitterbear.com/pages/shop-by-recipe).
- **Ratio:** Scofflaw Old Tom Gin: 4 parts; fresh lemon juice: 2 parts; semi-rich simple syrup (1.5:1 sugar:water): 1 part; soda water: 4-6 parts. 1 part = 1/2 US fl oz.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 2 fl oz (4 parts) - Scofflaw Old Tom Gin
- [ ] 1 fl oz (2 parts) - fresh lemon juice
- [ ] 1/2 fl oz (1 part) - semi-rich simple syrup (1.5:1 sugar:water)
- [ ] 2-3 fl oz (4-6 parts) - soda water
- [ ] Lemon wheel and cocktail cherry for garnish
- [ ] Ice, as needed for the mixing and serving steps below

## Instructions

1. Grab a Collins glass and fill it with ice.
2. In a shaker, combine the Old Tom Gin, fresh lemon juice, and semi-rich simple syrup.
3. Add ice to the shaker and shake until cold.
4. Strain into the prepared Collins glass over fresh ice.
5. Top with 2 to 3 fl oz of soda water.
6. Garnish with a lemon wheel and a cocktail cherry.

## Notes

# The Classic White Lady Recipe - Variation #1

- **Source:** House of Bitter Bear / Anders Erickson, [The Classic White Lady Recipe - Variation #1](https://houseofbitterbear.com/collections/the-classic-white-lady-recipe-variation-1). Accessed 2026-09-27.
- **Version:** Published source specification; instructions condensed. Quantity assumptions and source issues are noted below.
- **Yield:** 1 cocktail (serving assumption where the source omits yield).
- **Source video:** [Creator video linked by the publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IAmf7XqE0T8).
- **Ratio:** Plymouth Gin: 6 parts; Luxardo Triplum Triple Sec: 3 parts; fresh lemon juice: 3 parts; semi-rich simple syrup (1.5:1 sugar:water) OR 1:1 simple: 1 part. 1 part = 1/4 US fl oz.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 1/2 fl oz (6 parts) - Plymouth Gin
- [ ] 3/4 fl oz (3 parts) - Luxardo Triplum Triple Sec
- [ ] 3/4 fl oz (3 parts) - fresh lemon juice
- [ ] 1/4 fl oz (1 part) - semi-rich simple syrup (1.5:1 sugar:water) OR 1:1 simple
- [ ] Egg white from one small egg OR 3/4 fl oz (22.5 ml) aquafaba
- [ ] Ice, as needed for the mixing and serving steps below

## Instructions

1. Measure the gin, triple sec, fresh lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white (or aquafaba) into a shaker.
2. Dry shake for about 15-20 seconds to emulsify that egg white.
3. Add the ice to the shaker.
4. Shake it again, this time a wet shake, until chilled and diluted.
5. Double-strain into a chilled coupe or Nick & Nora glass.

## Notes

Use pasteurized eggs/egg products when served raw or undercooked ([FDA egg guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/what-you-need-know-about-egg-safety)). This is a safety clarification, not a source quantity change.

# Amaretto Sour

- **Source:** House of Bitter Bear / Anders Erickson, [Amaretto Sour](https://houseofbitterbear.com/collections/amaretto-sour). Accessed 2026-09-27.
- **Version:** Published source specification; instructions condensed. Quantity assumptions and source issues are noted below.
- **Yield:** 1 cocktail (serving assumption where the source omits yield).
- **Source video:** [Creator video linked by the publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_nIr7E-cMOs).
- **Ratio:** Luxardo Amaretto di Saschira: 6 parts; Laird's Straight Apple Brandy BIB: 3 parts; fresh lemon juice: 4 parts; rich Demerara syrup (2:1 sugar:water): 1 part; egg white OR aquafaba: 2 parts. 1 part = 1/4 US fl oz.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 1/2 fl oz (6 parts) - Luxardo Amaretto di Saschira
- [ ] 3/4 fl oz (3 parts) - Laird's Straight Apple Brandy BIB
- [ ] 1 fl oz (4 parts) - fresh lemon juice
- [ ] 1/4 fl oz (1 part) - rich Demerara syrup (2:1 sugar:water)
- [ ] 1/2 fl oz (2 parts) - egg white OR aquafaba
- [ ] Cocktail cherry for garnish
- [ ] Ice, as needed for the mixing and serving steps below

## Instructions

1. Measure amaretto, apple brandy, lemon juice, demerara syrup, and egg white (or aquafaba) into a shaker.
2. Dry shake vigorously for 10-15 seconds to emulsify.
3. Add ice to the shaker and wet shake until cold.
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe or sour glass.
5. Garnish with a cocktail cherry.

## Notes

Use pasteurized eggs/egg products when served raw or undercooked ([FDA egg guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/what-you-need-know-about-egg-safety)). This is a safety clarification, not a source quantity change.

Gluten status unresolved: verify Luxardo Amaretto di Saschira; egg white OR aquafaba; Cocktail cherry for garnish for gluten-avoiding guests. No gluten-free tag applied.

# The Alton Brown's Aged Eggnog Recipe (Half Portion)

- **Source:** House of Bitter Bear / Anders Erickson, [The Alton Brown's Aged Eggnog Recipe (Half Portion)](https://houseofbitterbear.com/collections/the-alton-browns-aged-eggnog-recipe-half-portion). Accessed 2026-09-27.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 6 egg yolks
- [ ] 1/2 pound sugar
- [ ] 1/2 tsp freshly grated nutmeg
- [ ] 8 fl oz (2 parts) - 1/2 & 1/2
- [ ] 8 fl oz (2 parts) - whole milk

- [ ] 1/8 tsp salt

## Instructions

1. In a large bowl, whisk together the egg yolks, sugar, 1/2 teaspoon nutmeg, and salt until combined and pale.
2. Gradually incorporate the 1/2 & 1/2, whole milk, and heavy cream, stirring until smooth.
3. Pour in the Appleton rum, Maison Rouge cognac, and Elijah Craig bourbon. Stir well to fully integrate the spirits.
4. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean, sealable container.
5. Transfer to the refrigerator promptly; see the aging limitation below before choosing a storage period.
6. To serve, pour into glasses and garnish with freshly grated nutmeg.

## Notes

Use pasteurized eggs/egg products when served raw or undercooked ([FDA egg guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/what-you-need-know-about-egg-safety)). This is a safety clarification, not a source quantity change.

# The Classic Old Fashioned (aka Spoon Cocktail)

- **Source:** House of Bitter Bear / Anders Erickson, [The Classic Old Fashioned (aka Spoon Cocktail)](https://houseofbitterbear.com/collections/the-classic-old-fashioned-aka-spoon-cocktail). Accessed 2026-09-27.
- **Version:** Published source specification; instructions condensed. Quantity assumptions and source issues are noted below.
- **Yield:** 1 cocktail (serving assumption where the source omits yield).
- **Source video:** [Creator video linked by the publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0rnil0_xFnM).

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 sugar cube
- [ ] Splash soda water
- [ ] 2 dashes Angostura Bitters
- [ ] 2 fl oz - Old Overholt Straight Rye Whiskey 86 proof
- [ ] Expressed lemon oil and peel
- [ ] Serve with a small spoon (optional)
- [ ] Ice, as needed for the mixing and serving steps below

## Instructions

1. Drop the sugar cube into an old fashioned glass. Add a small splash of soda water.
2. Gently muddle that sugar until mostly dissolved.
3. Add two dashes of Angostura bitters.
4. Pour in the two fl oz of Old Overholt Rye.
5. Add one large, clear ice cube.
6. Stir for about 20-30 seconds to get it chilled and diluted.
7. Squeeze a lemon peel over the drink to release its oils, then drop the peel right in.
8. Serve it, with a small spoon on the side if you like.

## Notes

# The Go-To Sherry Eggnog Recipe

# Sloe Gin Sour

- **Source:** House of Bitter Bear / Anders Erickson, [Sloe Gin Sour](https://houseofbitterbear.com/collections/sloe-gin-sour). Accessed 2026-09-27.
- **Version:** Published source specification; instructions condensed. Quantity assumptions and source issues are noted below.
- **Yield:** 1 cocktail (serving assumption where the source omits yield).
- **Recipe text:** [Publisher recipe index](https://houseofbitterbear.com/pages/shop-by-recipe).
- **Status:** Source clarification needed; see Notes before making.
- **Ratio:** Plymouth Sloe Gin: 3 parts; Campari: 1 part; fresh lemon juice: 1 1/2 parts; semi-rich simple syrup (1.5:1, sugar:water): 1 part. 1 part = 1/2 US fl oz.

## Ingredients

- [ ] 1 1/2 fl oz (3 parts) - Plymouth Sloe Gin
- [ ] 1/2 fl oz (1 part) - Campari
- [ ] 3/4 fl oz (1 1/2 parts) - fresh lemon juice
- [ ] 1/2 fl oz (1 part) - semi-rich simple syrup (1.5:1, sugar:water)
- [ ] 12/ fl oz. (15 ml) egg white OR aquafaba
- [ ] Expressed lemon oil and 3 drops of Angostura Bitters for garnish
- [ ] Ice, as needed for the mixing and serving steps below

## Instructions

1. Measure sloe gin, Campari, lemon juice, simple syrup, and egg white or aquafaba into a shaker.
2. Dry shake vigorously for 15 to 20 seconds.
3. Add ice to the shaker and wet shake until chilled.
4. Double strain into a chilled coupe or sour glass.
5. Squeeze lemon peel over the drink, then add three drops of Angostura bitters.

## Notes

Source typo: "12/ oz. (15 ml)" for egg white/aquafaba is not a usable ounce quantity. Confirm the intended measure before making.

Use pasteurized eggs/egg products when served raw or undercooked ([FDA egg guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/what-you-need-know-about-egg-safety)). This is a safety clarification, not a source quantity change.
